title: Digitaria ischaemum

{{Short description|Species of plant}} {{Speciesbox |image = Digitaria ischaemum 15-p.bot-digit.ischae-01.jpg |genus = Digitaria |species = ischaemum |authority = ([[Johann Christian Daniel von Schreber|Schreb.]]) Schreb. ex [[Gotthilf Heinrich Ernst Muhlenberg|Muhl.]] |synonyms = ''Panicum ischaemum''
''Syntherisma ischaemum'' }} [[File:Digitaria ischaemum syis 001 pvd.jpg|thumb|left|Illustration]] '''''Digitaria ischaemum''''' is a species of [[Digitaria|crabgrass]] known by the common names '''smooth crabgrass''' and '''small crabgrass'''.{{Cite web |title=Digitaria ischaemum {{!}} UMass Amherst Landscape, Nursery & Urban Forestry Program |url=https://extension.umass.edu/weed-herbarium/weeds/digitaria-ischaemum |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=extension.umass.edu}} It is native to Europe and Asia, but it is known throughout much of the warm temperate world as an [[introduced species]] and often a common roadside and garden weed. It is an annual grass producing an [[inflorescence]] with two or more narrow branches lined with tiny spikelets. It is easily confused with other members in the genus, particularly [[southern crabgrass]] in California which differs by having spikelets of nearly twice the length. It may also be confused with [[Bermuda Grass]], but differs in being a much taller plant with a much longer inflorescence.{{Cite web |title=OregonFlora |url=https://oregonflora.org/taxa/index.php?taxon=4566 |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=oregonflora.org}} It reproduces by seed. The leaves on this grass often form above the base of the plant, and it is usually singular, rarely forming large clumps. ==Description== The flowers of smooth crabgrass grow in clusters of 2 to 6, forming spike-like shapes about 1½ to 4 inches long, arranged like fingers at the tips of branching stems. The flower [[spikelet]]s are small, egg-shaped, and come in pairs along the stem, with one on a short stalk and the other on a longer one. Each spikelet has one fertile flower. The small bracts at the base of each spikelet are uneven in size, with one being almost invisible or absent and the other covered in short hairs. The bracts around the flowers are similarly sized, with one being hairy and the other having tiny pits. The flower styles and [[stamen]]s extend from the tip of the spikelet. The stem holding the spikes is green or purple, winged, and about 1 mm wide, with all the spikelets arranged on one side of the stem. The leaves of smooth crabgrass are arranged alternately, up to 4 inches long and ¼ inch wide, mostly flat and hairless except at the base. The leaf sheaths are open in the front, sometimes with a few long hairs near the top but mostly hairless, and they loosely wrap around the stem, often having a ridge along the back. The [[ligule]] is white and very short, less than 1 mm. The [[Plant stem|stems]] (culms) are hairless, branch out from the base, and are mostly light green but may be purple near the base. The stems often spread outward and may root at the joints (nodes), which are hairless and can be green or purplish. As smooth crabgrass matures, its spikelets turn dark purple. The missing first [[glume]] and the hairs on the second glume and [[Lemma (morphology)|lemma]] become more noticeable. The seeds are oval-shaped and dark brown to almost black.{{Cite web |title=Digitaria ischaemum (Smooth Crabgrass): Minnesota Wildflowers |url=https://www.minnesotawildflowers.info/grass-sedge-rush/smooth-crabgrass |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=www.minnesotawildflowers.info |language=en}} ==Habitat== They grow in terrestrial regions and can be seen in [[central Europe]] and [[Japan]], [[Connecticut]], [[Maine]], [[Massachusetts]], [[New Hampshire]], [[Rhode Island]], [[Vermont]].{{Cite web |title=Digitaria ischaemum (smooth crabgrass): Go Botany |url=https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/digitaria/ischaemum/ |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org}}{{Cite web |title=Digitaria ischaemum (Small Crabgrass, Smooth Crabgrass) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/digitaria-ischaemum/ |access-date=2024-10-25 |website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== * [http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_JM_treatment.pl?8738,8945,8946 Jepson Manual Treatment.] * [https://web.archive.org/web/20110611151635/http://herbarium.usu.edu/webmanual/info2.asp?name=Digitaria_ischaemum&type=treatment Grass Manual Treatment] * {{CalPhotos|Digitaria|ischaemum}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q159824}} [[Category:Digitaria|ischaemum]] [[Category:Grasses of Asia]] [[Category:Grasses of Europe]] {{Panicoideae-stub}}
